title: Unvalidated Custom Endpoint Base URL Allowed Arbitrary Cloud Metadata SSRF
reproduction_steps: Configure an OpenAI-compatible provider with base_url='http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/'. An outbound HTTP request was previously issued to AWS/Azure metadata services.
evidence: SSRF vulnerability verified prior to Phase 6 hardening.
residual_risk: Low. Scheme and IP/hostname checks strictly reject link-local and cloud metadata destinations while allowing local development on localhost/127.0.0.1.

title: Raw HTTPX Network and Auth Exceptions Could Bubble Up Unnormalized
reproduction_steps: Simulate connection timeout, socket error, or HTTP 401/429/500 from LLM endpoint. Without normalization, internal socket details and stack traces could be exposed to callers.
evidence: Observed unmapped httpx.ConnectTimeout in direct provider calls.
residual_risk: None. Structured exception hierarchy (LLMTimeoutError, LLMConnectionError, LLMAuthenticationError, LLMRateLimitError, LLMProviderError) normalizes all provider errors.

title: Assistant Model and Provider Fields Lacked Server-Side Whitelisting
reproduction_steps: Create or update an assistant with default_model='' or llm_provider='unsupported_arbitrary_backend'. Was previously accepted and caused late failures during conversation streaming.
evidence: Unconstrained string fields in Assistant model allowed arbitrary inputs.
residual_risk: None. Strict whitelist {'omniroute', 'openai', 'mock'} and non-empty model checks enforced at repository level.

title: Empty Response Stream from LLM Provider Could Commit Blank Messages
reproduction_steps: If an upstream provider returns zero tokens before finishing, an empty assistant Message record could be inserted and committed to the database.
evidence: Stream completion previously committed final_content without validating whether any non-whitespace tokens were generated.
residual_risk: None. AssistantRuntime now intercepts empty final content, emits message_error, and prevents database write.
